summary: Defines a Time Sliding Window Three Colour Marker, which can be used as a component in a Differentiated Services traffic conditioner. It marks packets with one of three colours according to how fast a flow is sending. It is an experimental protocol.

plainLanguage.summary: A meter watches how fast someone sends and paints each packet green, yellow or red, depending on whether they are within their limit.

when should i use tswtcm in diffserv
subtitle: A traffic marker that colors packets green, yellow or red to show sending rate relative to a contract.

tldr.problem: Network operators need a way to classify packets when traffic exceeds agreed speeds, and do so without dropping multiple packets from the same TCP flow, which would hurt throughput.
tldr.mechanism: TSWTCM runs two processes: one estimates a traffic flow's sending rate over time, and another marks each packet as green (within contracted rate), yellow (between two rate limits), or red (exceeding peak rate) using probabilities that correspond to the excess traffic.
tldr.outcome: Routers using Assured Forwarding can treat red packets as most droppable, yellow as intermediate, and green as least droppable, providing tiered quality of service. The experiment did not see wide adoption.

facts.label: Rate parameters
facts.value: Committed Target Rate (CTR), Peak Target Rate (PTR)

today: RFC 2859 defines an experimental protocol for traffic marking that was not widely adopted. DiffServ implementations typically use simpler marker algorithms. The RFC is still an Internet standard for reference, but TSWTCM has not seen deployment as a primary traffic conditioner.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
The Time Sliding Window Three Colour Marker (TSWTCM) marks individual packets with one of three colours based on how fast the traffic stream is sending compared to two rate limits. These limits are the Committed Target Rate (CTR), the rate the customer has paid for, and the Peak Target Rate (PTR), a burst rate above that.

Packets sending at or below the CTR get marked green. Packets in the part of the traffic between CTR and PTR get marked yellow. Packets causing the rate to exceed PTR get marked red. TSWTCM is designed for use with the Assured Forwarding Per Hop Behaviour (AF PHB) in DiffServ, where each colour maps to a drop precedence level in the router.

A key design choice is to mark using probability rather than deterministic rules. This protects TCP flows from losing multiple packets in the same window, which would reduce throughput.
sections.plainLanguage: TSWTCM watches the rate at which data arrives. If it is going slow, paint green. If it is between two limits, paint yellow with some chance. If it is over the top limit, paint red with some chance. This way, routers know what to drop first when busy.

sections.title: How TSWTCM Works
sections.content:
TSWTCM has two independent parts. A rate estimator measures the running average bandwidth of the traffic stream, smoothing out burstiness to approximate the longer-term sending rate. A marker then assigns a colour to each packet using that estimate.

The rate estimator can use different algorithms (such as exponential weighted moving average or time-based filters) as long as they yield similar results over a time window called AVG_INTERVAL. Preferably, it tracks time-based history rather than weight-based history, so that fast flows do not decay their history faster than slow flows.

The marker uses a probabilistic function to decide the colour. When the rate is between CTR and PTR, the probability of yellow marking is the fraction of the traffic above CTR. When the rate exceeds PTR, probability of red is the fraction above PTR, probability of yellow is the fraction between CTR and PTR, and the remainder is green. This probabilistic approach reduces the chance that multiple packets from the same flow are marked red or yellow.
sections.plainLanguage: The estimator measures how much data arrived recently, smoothed out so bursts do not fool it. The marker then rolls dice to paint each packet, so the chance of painting it red or yellow matches how much the traffic is over its limit.

sections.title: Configuration
sections.content:
TSWTCM configuration centers on two parameters: the CTR and PTR. The PTR MUST be equal to or greater than the CTR. Both MAY be expressed in bits per second or bytes per second.

For the rate estimator, the AVG_INTERVAL time window should be configurable. Recommendations from the RFC suggest using an interval roughly equal to the round-trip time for a single TCP flow, or 1 second for aggregates with multiple TCP flows or mixed TCP and UDP traffic. If weight-based estimation is used, the WEIGHT factor becomes configurable.

Special cases exist: if PTR equals CTR, TSWTCM operates with a single rate and packets are marked only green or red, never yellow. If PTR is set to link speed and CTR is below that, packets are marked only green or yellow, never red. The rate estimator measures IP header and payload but does not include link-layer headers.
sections.plainLanguage: You set two numbers: the promised rate and the burst limit. You can also pick how far back in time the meter looks to calculate the average. Different trade-offs let you tune for single TCP flows or large aggregates.

sections.title: The Marking Algorithm
sections.content:
The marker operates in the router forwarding path and implements the following rules:

If the estimated average rate is less than or equal to CTR, all packets are marked green.

If the average rate is greater than CTR but at or below PTR, packets are marked yellow with probability P0 and green with probability (1-P0), where P0 is the fraction (avg-rate - CTR) / avg-rate.

If the average rate exceeds PTR, packets are marked red with probability P1, yellow with probability P2, and green with probability (1 - P1 - P2), where P1 is the fraction (avg-rate - PTR) / avg-rate and P2 is the fraction (PTR - CTR) / avg-rate.

This algorithm ensures that when the traffic is within contract, green packets dominate. When it is over contract, the excess traffic is distributed probabilistically among yellow and red, in proportions matching how much the rate has exceeded each threshold.
sections.plainLanguage: The algorithm uses simple math: divide the excess traffic by the total traffic to get the chance of painting the packet yellow or red. This way, if the flow sends 20% over limit, about 20% of its packets get painted yellow.

sections.title: Use in Services
sections.content:
TSWTCM works with any type of traffic stream: single TCP flows, aggregates of TCP flows, and mixes of TCP and UDP. When used with Assured Forwarding, a service provider can offer tiered service based on drop probability. Packets marked green have the highest chance of delivery, yellow are intermediate, and red have the lowest.

With sufficient over-provisioning of the network, customers are mostly assured of achieving their CTR. Traffic between CTR and PTR has lesser assurance. Traffic above PTR has the least assurance due to high drop probability of red packets.

This allows the service provider to charge customers on a sliding scale: one price for CTR delivery, a lower price for PTR delivery, and rates in between for the intermediate tier.
sections.plainLanguage: Operators can promise to deliver all green packets and most yellow packets, but only some red ones. By offering different prices for each tier, they can give customers what they pay for.
